request: Build a custom inference engine for Meta Muse Spark Open that runs on NVIDIA DGX Spark. The attached System Ontology files describe the model, the machine and the target the engine is judged on. Take them as the statement of what is wanted.

documents.name: target.yaml
documents.text:
kind: engine_spec
id: spec/muse-spark-open-on-dgx-spark/target
title: "First use case: a custom inference engine for Meta Muse Spark Open on NVIDIA DGX Spark"
spec_level: target
ontology_version: 0.6.1
# What the scope page states is written with its source. What the scope page leaves undefined but an engine cannot be
# judged without is written as a proposal (status: proposed) so that it can be confirmed or replaced. What only the
# project can decide stays UNSET. Fields left to the factory are `open`.

given:
  model: model/muse-spark-open
  hardware: hw/dgx-spark
  environment: UNSET

boundary:
  form: UNSET                    # execution library, offline engine or online service
  packaging: {value: container, resolution: required, source: "scope-slide#initial-scope"}

interface:
  input:  {modality: text, resolution: required, source: "scope-slide#initial-scope"}
  output: {modality: text, resolution: required, source: "scope-slide#initial-scope"}
  streaming: UNSET

execution: open
state: open
composition: open
policy: open
binding: open

contract:
  requirements:
    - id: c-mem
      quantity: memory_budget
      kind: pass_fail
      status: proposed
      value: 80
      unit: GB
      unit_basis: decimal
      pool: mem0
      accounting_boundary: "Everything the engine's container holds in the unified pool at any moment: allocations of the process on CPU and GPU, and page cache attributable to the files it reads. The operating system and other processes are outside."
      source: "scope-slide#memory: Strata-Spark: 80 GB Unified Memory"
      note: "The scope page names three figures. 128 GB is the machine's nominal memory, of which 121.6 GB is reported allocatable, so it cannot be a budget. 12 GB is called a GPU working-set figure, and this machine has no separate GPU memory to apply it to. 80 GB is the one figure that is a budget for this machine. The choice, the unit basis and the accounting boundary are proposals to be confirmed."
    - id: c-context
      quantity: context_length
      kind: pass_fail
      value: UNSET
      unit: tokens
      note: "The model allows 1,000,000 tokens. The attention state for the offered context is taken from the same 80 GB as the expert cache, so the engine cannot be sized until this is given. The scope page does not give it."
    - id: c-quality
      quantity: quality_score
      kind: pass_fail
      status: proposed
      baseline: "The published reference implementation with the NVFP4 weights, the published tokenizer and greedy sampling."
      comparison: "If no change to the computation is allowed: the same output tokens as the baseline. Otherwise: a task score not below the threshold."
      taskset: UNSET             # scope page: held-out task set, not named
      threshold: UNSET           # scope page: pass threshold to be decided
      source: "scope-slide#quality: fixed reference baseline"
    - id: c-ttft
      quantity: ttft
      kind: report
      status: proposed
      timing_start: "The engine admits the request. Model load is excluded."
      timing_end: "The first output token is produced by the engine."
      workload: UNSET
    - id: c-decode
      quantity: decode_rate
      kind: report
      status: proposed
      includes_first_token: false
      workload: UNSET
    - id: c-peak
      quantity: peak_memory
      kind: report
      status: proposed
      pool: mem0
      accounting_boundary: "The same boundary as c-mem."
      workload: UNSET
  allowed_transformations: UNSET # whether quantisation below NVFP4 or approximations that change output are allowed
  workload: UNSET                # scope page: a fixed workload, not defined. Prompt lengths decide the time to first token.

delivery:
  model_checkpoint: UNSET        # scope page: one checkpoint. The model card offers BF16 and NVFP4; only NVFP4 is within reach.
  deliverables:
    - {item: reproducible_container, resolution: required}
    - {item: clean_rebuild,          resolution: required}
    - {item: benchmark_report,       resolution: required}
    - {item: replayable_run_artifacts, resolution: required}

documents.name: model.yaml
documents.text:
kind: model
id: model/muse-spark-open
title: "Meta Muse Spark Open (816B parameters in total, 42B active per token)"
default_status: vendor_stated
note: "Structure figures are from Meta's model card (https://huggingface.co/meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B) and release post (https://research.meta.ai/blog/muse-spark-open), read 2026-11-10. config.json needs a login and was not read. The card does not give the size of the expert weights and of the other weights separately, nor the size on disk; the sizes below are derived from the card's totals under one stated assumption. The card mentions no draft head, no always-on shared expert and no state other than attention; only what the card states is described."
operations:
  - id: expert_router
    kind: selection
    selects: {operation: expert_ffn, out_of: 256, pick: 8, per: "token per layer"}
  - id: expert_ffn
    kind: compute
    reads: [expert_weights]
  - id: shared_blocks
    kind: compute
    reads: [shared_weights, token_embedding]
    writes: [attention_kv]
  - id: output_projection
    kind: compute
    reads: [output_head_weights]
    note: "The projection to the vocabulary of 202,048 tokens."
  - id: perception_encoder
    kind: compute
    serves_modality: [image, video, audio]
    reads: [encoder_weights]
data:
  - id: expert_weights
    kind: weight
    partitioned_by: [layer, expert]          # 62 layers x 256 = 15,872 experts
    encoded_bits: 4
    size:
      value: 399.5
      unit: GB
      unit_basis: decimal
      status: derived
      note: "Assumes the 42B active parameters are all the non-expert parameters plus 8 of 256 experts per layer. Then experts E and the rest S satisfy E + S = 816B and E/32 + S = 42B, giving E = 799.0B and S = 17.0B. At 4 bits per parameter (NVFP4) the experts are 399.5 GB, about 25.2 MB each. The true value is in the weight file headers."
  - id: shared_weights
    kind: weight
    size:
      value: 8.5
      unit: GB
      unit_basis: decimal
      status: derived
      note: "17.0B non-expert parameters under the same assumption, at 4 bits. It includes the embedding table and the output head. If these are kept at 16 bits the figure is 34 GB."
  - id: token_embedding
    kind: weight
    note: "202,048 rows of 8,192 values: 1.66B parameters, counted inside shared_weights."
  - id: output_head_weights
    kind: weight
    note: "Counted inside shared_weights. Whether it is tied to the embedding table is not stated on the card."
  - id: encoder_weights
    kind: weight
  - {id: attention_kv, kind: model_state, note: "Its size per token is not on the card. If keys and values are as wide as the hidden size and kept at 16 bits, it is 2.0 MB per token over 62 layers, so 65 GB for a context of 32,768 tokens. Grouped or compressed attention would lower this several times. It must be read from config.json."}
statements:
  - {subject: model/muse-spark-open, property: params_total,            value: 816e9, status: vendor_stated, source: "hf-model-card#overview"}
  - {subject: model/muse-spark-open, property: params_active_per_token, value: 42e9,  status: vendor_stated, source: "hf-model-card#overview"}
  - {subject: model/muse-spark-open, property: layers,                  value: 62,    status: vendor_stated, source: "hf-model-card#language-model"}
  - {subject: model/muse-spark-open, property: hidden_dim,              value: 8192,  status: vendor_stated, source: "hf-model-card#language-model"}
  - {subject: model/muse-spark-open, property: vocab_size,              value: 202048, status: vendor_stated, source: "hf-model-card#overview"}
  - {subject: model/muse-spark-open, property: context_length,          value: 1000000, status: vendor_stated, source: "hf-model-card#overview"}
  - {subject: model/muse-spark-open, property: modality_in,             value: "text+image+video+audio", status: vendor_stated, source: "hf-model-card#overview"}
  - {subject: model/muse-spark-open, property: modality_out,            value: text,  status: vendor_stated, source: "hf-model-card#overview"}
  - {subject: model/muse-spark-open, property: weight_precisions,       value: "BF16, NVFP4", status: vendor_stated, source: "hf-model-card#weights"}
  - {subject: model/muse-spark-open, property: checkpoint_format,       value: safetensors, status: vendor_stated, source: "hf-model-card#files"}
  - {subject: model/muse-spark-open, property: vram_required, value: 700,  unit: GB, status: vendor_stated, source: "hf-model-card#weights", conditions: {precision: NVFP4}}
  - {subject: model/muse-spark-open, property: vram_required, value: 2000, unit: GB, status: vendor_stated, source: "hf-model-card#weights", conditions: {precision: BF16}}
  - {subject: model/muse-spark-open, property: license,                 value: "Muse Model License", status: vendor_stated, source: "hf-model-card#license"}

node-types.yaml
documents.text:
# DRAFT 0.9 (2026-11-17). Generic node types of an inference engine: the node level of the System Ontology.
#
# A node type describes a kind of engine part, independent of any engine and any machine. It states what the part
# promises, not how it is built. It holds no parameter values, no call interfaces and no source references.
# One part of an engine may realise two node types; a node type is a job, not a module boundary.
#
# Written by `tools/so_nodetypes.py thin` from the frozen draft 0.8 (validation/heldout/node-types.draft-0.8.yaml)
# and validation/thin/amendments-0.9.yaml. Do not edit by hand: change the amendments and run the tool again.
# Draft 0.8 keeps what was removed here: the causes behind each effect on output, how engines relax the `should`
# rules, and every choice seen in a single engine (validation/choices/recurrence.yaml lists them with their engine).
#
# Fields of a node type
#   group             the group of node types it belongs to (see `groups`)
#   summary           the one job
#   not               what is easily mistaken for its job
#   needed_when       the property of the model, the machine or the service that makes the node necessary; absent
#                     when every engine has it
#   forms             distinct ways engines realise it, when there is more than one
#   takes, gives      what it consumes and produces. Which node it connects to differs between engines and is
#                     stated at system level, not here.
#   owns_state        what it alone keeps consistent
#   effect_on_output  the levels (see `effect_levels`) the node's own work can reach. The first four are the
#                     equivalence levels of the format, so they compare directly with a target's
#                     `allowed_transformations`.
#   indirect_effect   true when the node decides something other nodes' effects depend on (see `output_principles`)
#   rules             what the node guarantees; `must` or `should` (see `rule_strengths` and `rule_scope`)
#   choices           what is left for whoever builds the engine to decide. Names only, no values. Listed only when
#                     at least `choices_kept_when.engines` of the engines examined decide it; `engines` is how many.
#   seen_in           the engines examined that have a part of this type
draft_version: '0.9'
derived_from: draft 0.8, frozen 2026-11-16
engines_examined: [strata, ds4, hyperqwen, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
choices_kept_when:
  engines: 2
  of: 6
effect_levels:
- id: bit_exact
  meaning: The same tokens, bit for bit.
- id: numeric
  meaning: Logits differ in their last bits. A greedy token can occasionally flip and a sampled draw can differ; quality
    is not expected to change.
- id: distribution_exact
  meaning: Under sampling, the same distribution but a different draw for the same seed.
- id: approximate
  meaning: A deliberate change to the computation or to stored precision. Quality can change. It is asked for, or it is
    a default of the engine that can be turned off.
- id: defines
  meaning: 'The node decides what the input or the returned output is, by design: the template, the sampling settings, a
    constraint, where output stops.'
rule_strengths:
- id: must
  meaning: Kept by every engine examined, within `rule_scope`.
- id: should
  meaning: A correctness rule that some engines examined relax. An engine that relaxes it says so.
rule_scope: Rules bind every mode whose output is meant to be used. A mode that is turned on explicitly for measurement
  or debugging, and whose output the engine declares not valid, is outside them; such a mode is off by default and visible
  in the run's settings.
output_principles:
- '`effect_on_output` is what a node''s own work does: its arithmetic, the precision it stores, the content it writes. A
  node with `indirect_effect` also changes output through other nodes, by deciding something their effects depend on: how
  wide a step is, where a prompt is cut, which device computes, what is resident, what stored state survives, which setting
  is on. It then reaches the levels of the nodes it acts through.'
- Anything that changes how the computation is cut is at least `numeric`. It reaches `approximate` where kernels pick activation
  precision by the shape of a step, or where a node omits work by default under a condition another node sets.
- Stored state reused in place of recomputation carries the rounding and precision of the step that produced it, not of
  the step that would have recomputed it.
groups:
- id: preparation
  title: Preparation
  about: 'What is done before the engine starts serving: converting the model''s files and measuring what later choices
    rest on.'
- id: startup
  title: Startup
  about: Loading the model and dividing the machine's resources before the first request.
- id: computation
  title: Computation
  about: Carrying out the model's arithmetic on the machine's devices.
- id: selective-weights
  title: Selectively used weights
  about: 'For models that use only some of their weights per token (experts, lookup rows): keeping the right ones within
    reach.'
- id: sequence-state
  title: Sequence state
  about: What the engine remembers per sequence, where it is kept, and how it is reused.
- id: speculation
  title: Speculation
  about: Proposing several tokens cheaply and having the full model check them.
- id: token-output
  title: Token output
  about: Turning logits into the tokens and text that are returned.
- id: serving
  title: Serving
  about: Everything between a client request and a step of the engine.
- id: multi-device
  title: Several devices
  about: One model spread over several devices or machines.
- id: operations
  title: Operations
  about: Settings, limits while running, and records of what happened.
types:
- id: model-conversion
  group: preparation
  summary: 'Offline, obtain, pin and record the published model and produce the files this engine reads: weights in the
    engine''s layout and precision where conversion is offline, and any derived pieces such as a reduced draft head or a
    corrected chat template.'
  not: It does nothing while the engine serves.
  needed_when: The engine does not read the published files as they are, or it needs pieces derived from them.
  takes:
  - the published checkpoint, tokenizer and template
  - calibration data, when precision is changed
  gives:
  - the engine's model files
  - a record of what was converted and how
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact, numeric, distribution_exact, approximate, defines]
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: 'An interrupted or mismatched conversion is never accepted as complete: it is written under a temporary name until
      finished, or it is rejected when loaded.'
  choices:
  - what: precision per kind of weight, and per layer where it differs
    engines: 4
  - what: which derived pieces are built (draft head, shortlist vocabulary, extra copies), and their size
    engines: 3
  - what: which source formats and architecture constants a recipe accepts
    engines: 2
  seen_in: [ds4, hyperqwen, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: calibration
  group: preparation
  summary: Measure the model or the machine offline, at startup, or during an opt-in profiling run, and record results that
    other nodes take as fixed input.
  forms:
  - usage statistics of selectively used weights
  - cost or speed fits for a machine
  - statistics for lossy conversion
  - a split ratio between two devices
  takes:
  - the model and a set of prompts, or timings on the machine
  gives:
  - 'recorded data: usage rankings, cost fits, statistics for quantisation, per-machine settings'
  owns_state:
  - the recorded results and, where the engine keeps one, the key that says what they are valid for
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact]
  indirect_effect: true
  rules:
  - strength: should
    rule: A recorded result is used only where its validity key matches the model, machine and build.
  choices:
  - what: what is measured and on which prompts
    engines: 3
  - what: 'the rule that accepts or rejects a measured result: the noise tolerated and the least gain it must predict'
    engines: 3
  - what: how much data a measurement collects
    engines: 2
  seen_in: [strata, ds4, hyperqwen, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: model-loading
  group: startup
  summary: At startup, and again whenever released weights are restored, open the model's files, check they are something
    this engine can run, and make the weights every token uses readable by the computation.
  not: It does not decide how much memory each consumer gets; memory planning does.
  takes:
  - the engine's model files
  - a placement plan
  gives:
  - resident weights
  - the model's shape and tensor directory
  - where selectively used weights lie in the files
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact, numeric, distribution_exact, approximate]
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: A file whose declared shape the kernels cannot run is refused, not loaded.
  choices:
  - what: map the file in place or copy into memory
    engines: 2
  - what: which tensors go to which memory or device
    engines: 3
  - what: whether weights are re-encoded at load and how
    engines: 3
  - what: what is done when a file is the wrong version, incomplete or of an unsupported shape
    engines: 2
  - what: staging buffers and reader threads used while loading
    engines: 2
  - what: which stored encoding of a tensor is loaded when the files carry more than one, and which kernels accept it
    engines: 2
  seen_in: [strata, ds4, hyperqwen, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: memory-planning
  group: startup
  summary: At startup, divide the memory budget among resident weights, per-sequence state, working space, reserves and
    caches, and refuse to start when the minimum does not fit.
  takes:
  - the budget and the operator's limits
  - the model's shape
  - what the machine reports as its capacity or as free
  gives:
  - sizes for caches, state pools and work areas
  - which large parts stay in memory and which are streamed
  - the context length and concurrency the engine can offer, or the check that the requested ones fit
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact]
  indirect_effect: true
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: A computed plan that exceeds a hard limit is corrected or refused before the engine serves.
  - strength: should
    rule: A size the operator fixes by hand is checked against what was measured, or reported as unchecked.
  choices:
  - what: the reserve left free
    engines: 3
  - what: the order in which things are given up when memory is short, and when starting is refused
    engines: 2
  - what: an operator's explicit size against the computed one
    engines: 2
  - what: the least a cache may be and still work
    engines: 2
  seen_in: [strata, ds4, hyperqwen, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: graph-capture
  group: startup
  summary: 'Prepare the computation for fast repeated execution: compile kernels, warm up, and record execution graphs for
    the step shapes the engine will run.'
  needed_when: The device benefits from pre-recorded or pre-compiled work, or first-use compilation would stall a request.
  takes:
  - the loaded model
  - the step shapes that can occur
  gives:
  - compiled kernels and recorded graphs ready to replay
  owns_state:
  - compiled kernels and recorded graphs
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact, numeric]
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: A recorded graph is not replayed after the addresses or shapes it fixed have changed.
  - strength: should
    rule: A step shape or feature combination a recorded graph mishandles is refused at configuration.
  choices:
  - what: which step shapes are recorded ahead and which on first use
    engines: 2
  seen_in: [strata, ds4, hyperqwen, ninfer, llama-cpp]
- id: layer-compute
  group: computation
  summary: 'Compute what the model defines: embedding, attention of every kind the model has, recurrent layers, feed-forward
    blocks, expert selection and the selected experts, and the projection to the vocabulary.'
  takes:
  - the tokens of the step
  - resident weights
  - per-sequence state
  - weights or rows brought in for this step
  gives:
  - updated per-sequence state
  - logits
  - hidden features other nodes ask for
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact, numeric, approximate]
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: Unless an approximation is in effect that was turned on at conversion or at run time, explicitly or as a default
      that can be turned off, the sequence of layers and operations the model defines is kept. Otherwise only the order
      of accumulation inside one operation may vary.
  - strength: should
    rule: An approximation that is in effect is stated with the run's settings.
  choices:
  - what: which operations are fused
    engines: 2
  - what: activation precision inside kernels
    engines: 2
  - what: working space a kernel may hold, allocated ahead or during steps
    engines: 2
  seen_in: [strata, ds4, hyperqwen, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: device-backend
  group: computation
  summary: 'Drive a device for a step''s work: submit it, report results and retirement in order, and choose the kernel
    variant for the device and step shape where the computation does not.'
  takes:
  - the work of one step
  - what the device is
  gives:
  - submitted commands
  - completion and retirement signals
  owns_state:
  - device buffers and what is in flight
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact, numeric, approximate]
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: Memory still read by submitted work is not released or reused.
  choices:
  - what: how a kernel variant is chosen per device and step shape
    engines: 2
  seen_in: [ds4, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: secondary-compute
  group: computation
  summary: Compute a share of a layer's work on a second device, from weights it can read where they lie or that are prepared
    for it ahead of the layer.
  needed_when: A second device can compute something sooner than moving its inputs to the main device, or has spare capacity
    the main device lacks.
  forms:
  - selected experts on the CPU
  - a share of a dense block on another accelerator
  takes:
  - the share of work assigned to it
  - weights readable by the second device
  gives:
  - partial results merged into the layer's output
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact, numeric, approximate]
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: Weights handed to it stay readable for the whole of its computation.
  choices:
  - what: how work is cut into jobs, and their size
    engines: 3
  - what: what is done when it hangs or falls behind
    engines: 2
  - what: how idle workers wait
    engines: 2
  seen_in: [strata, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: model-edit
  group: computation
  summary: Apply a deliberate, optional change to the model's computation at run time, such as adding or removing a direction
    in its activations.
  needed_when: The engine offers run-time changes to the model's behaviour.
  takes:
  - the edit and its strength
  gives:
  - a changed computation
  effect_on_output: [approximate]
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: An edit is applied only when asked for, and its use is visible in the run's settings.
  seen_in: [ds4, llama-cpp]
- id: step-execution
  group: computation
  summary: 'Carry one planned step through the model: a decode step, a verify block or a prompt chunk, for one sequence
    or for several sharing the step.'
  takes:
  - the plan of one step
  - per-sequence state
  gives:
  - logits or accepted tokens for each sequence in the step
  - updated state
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact, numeric, approximate]
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: A step's results are used only after the work that produces them is complete.
  - strength: must
    rule: A step's memory is reused only after all of its device work has retired.
  choices:
  - what: which kinds of step are replayed from a recorded graph and which are launched directly
    engines: 2
  seen_in: [strata, ds4, hyperqwen, ninfer, llama-cpp]
- id: prompt-reading
  group: computation
  summary: Read a prompt in chunks, faster than token by token, and leave behind the state generation continues from.
  needed_when: The engine reads prompts by a path of its own. Engines that put prompt chunks and decode rows in the same
    step have no separate node.
  takes:
  - prompt tokens
  - the position reading starts from
  gives:
  - per-sequence state up to the end of the prompt
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact, numeric, approximate]
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: Unless an approximation is in effect that was turned on explicitly or as a default that can be turned off, the
      state it leaves is the state of that prompt up to rounding, whatever the chunking. Where activation precision follows
      the width of a chunk, it is that state up to that precision.
  - strength: should
    rule: Where chunk boundaries change stored state, reuse of that state either keys on the chunking or is declared to
      differ in rounding from a fresh read.
  choices:
  - what: chunk size
    engines: 3
  seen_in: [strata, ds4, ninfer, splash]
- id: media-preparation
  group: computation
  summary: Fetch, decode and prepare input that is not text (images, video, documents) into the form the model's encoder
    takes.
  needed_when: The engine serves input other than text.
  takes:
  - media or references to media from the request
  gives:
  - prepared media, with an identity later nodes can cache on
  owns_state:
  - cache of prepared media
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact, defines]
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: Media is not fetched or decoded outside the limits set for size, time and origin.
  choices:
  - what: limits on size, time and where media may be fetched from
    engines: 3
  seen_in: [ds4, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: modality-encoding
  group: computation
  summary: Run the model's encoder for input that is not text and produce the embeddings the model takes in its place.
  needed_when: The model accepts input other than text and the engine serves it.
  takes:
  - prepared media
  gives:
  - embedding rows placed in the prompt
  owns_state:
  - encoded media held until consumed, and a cache of it where one exists
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact, numeric, approximate, defines]
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: Embeddings are placed at the positions the prompt reserves for them.
  choices:
  - what: the largest input the encoder accepts, and how many embedding rows one prompt may carry
    engines: 2
  - what: whether the encoder is loaded at all, and whether its working memory is built only when media waits
    engines: 2
  seen_in: [ds4, hyperqwen, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: expert-source
  group: selective-weights
  summary: Keep every selectively used weight obtainable for the whole run from the slow place where all of them are held.
  needed_when: The model selects a few of many weight blocks per token, and they do not all sit in the memory the computation
    reads.
  takes:
  - where each one lies in the files
  gives:
  - the bytes of any requested one
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact]
  indirect_effect: true
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: What it delivers is complete; a partial read is an error, never reported as ready.
  choices:
  - what: how much of the full set is made directly readable by a device, and which part first
    engines: 2
  seen_in: [strata, ninfer]
- id: expert-cache
  group: selective-weights
  summary: Hold as many selectively used weights in fast memory as its budget allows, and answer for any of them whether
    it is there and where.
  not: Which blocks are kept is decided by the residency policy. The cache may still arrange, compact and pin what it holds.
  needed_when: Not all selectively used weights fit in fast memory, or a copy in fast memory is faster to compute from.
  takes:
  - its size
  - incoming weights
  - changes to its contents
  gives:
  - 'for each requested block: its slot, or that it is absent'
  owns_state:
  - which block is in which slot
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact]
  indirect_effect: true
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: Every reader of a block is ordered after the arrival of all its bytes, by completion or by the ordering of the
      stream.
  - strength: must
    rule: A slot is not overwritten while a computation may still read it.
  seen_in: [strata, ds4, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: residency-policy
  group: selective-weights
  summary: 'Decide which selectively used weights, or other blocks read back from slower storage into a bounded fast cache,
    are kept in fast memory: at startup from a ranking, or while running from use or from the size of the coming work.'
  needed_when: There is a cache of selectively used weights.
  forms:
  - fixed at startup from an offline ranking
  - adjusted while running from use counts
  - a preloaded list
  - regions switched by the size of the coming work between extra cache and streaming space
  takes:
  - how often each is used, a ranking made offline, or the size of the coming work
  gives:
  - what enters and what leaves
  owns_state:
  - the use history it decides from (use counts, or recency lists with remembered evictions), the ranking, or the current
    role of each region
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact]
  indirect_effect: true
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: A change of contents never makes a block unavailable to a computation already started.
  choices:
  - what: how use counts age, so that recent use outweighs old use
    engines: 2
  seen_in: [strata, ds4, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: expert-fetch
  group: selective-weights
  summary: Bring absent selectively used weights into fast memory, in an order the computation that follows can rely on.
  needed_when: There is a cache of selectively used weights.
  forms:
  - fetches a computation waits for
  - best-effort warming ahead of need
  takes:
  - requests for absent blocks
  - their bytes from the source
  gives:
  - the blocks in fast memory, and a signal when each is ready
  owns_state:
  - what is staged or in flight
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact, numeric]
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: A fetch a computation depends on is complete before that computation starts. Best-effort warming carries no such
      obligation.
  choices:
  - what: copies made one by one or batched
    engines: 2
  seen_in: [strata, ds4, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: expert-dispatch
  group: selective-weights
  summary: 'For each layer of each step, decide how every selected block gets computed: from fast memory, after a fetch,
    by another device, or not at all.'
  needed_when: Selected blocks can be in more than one place or computed by more than one device.
  takes:
  - which blocks each token selected
  - what is resident
  gives:
  - a plan for the layer
  - fetch requests
  - use counts
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact, numeric, approximate]
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: Every selected block that is not deliberately omitted is computed exactly once in the step that selected it.
  choices:
  - what: the share of misses fetched now against left to another device
    engines: 2
  seen_in: [strata, ds4, ninfer, llama-cpp]
- id: row-source
  group: selective-weights
  summary: Serve the rows of a large table that each token needs, without holding the whole table in fast memory.
  needed_when: The model has a table too large to hold whole in fast memory, of which each token reads a few rows.
  takes:
  - the row numbers for the coming tokens, or the recent tokens they are computed from
  - the table on storage
  gives:
  - the rows, before the layer that uses them
  owns_state:
  - 'where the node keeps them: a row cache, and the recent tokens the row numbers are computed from'
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact]
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: The rows delivered for a token are the rows that token's keys name.
  choices:
  - what: row cache
    engines: 3
  - what: warming the table in the background and when to stop
    engines: 2
  seen_in: [strata, ds4, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: storage-reader
  group: selective-weights
  summary: Run the engine's reads from storage for every node that needs them, so that reads the current step depends on
    go ahead of reads made ahead of need.
  needed_when: Several kinds of data are read from the same storage while the engine runs.
  takes:
  - read requests from several nodes
  gives:
  - the bytes read, and failures
  owns_state:
  - queued and in-flight reads
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact]
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: A read the current step waits for is not delayed behind reads made ahead of need.
  - strength: must
    rule: A failed or short read is reported to the node that asked, never passed on as data.
  seen_in: [splash]
- id: positional-state-store
  group: sequence-state
  summary: Hold the state a model keeps per position (attention keys and values, and any compressed or indexed form of them),
    in the format chosen for storage. This covers the served model and any secondary model, such as a draft model, that
    keeps state per position.
  not: Handing out, sharing and compacting the pages state lives in is the state pool's job where one exists.
  takes:
  - new state from the computation
  - how much it may hold
  gives:
  - past state to the computation
  owns_state:
  - per-position state of each sequence
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact, numeric, approximate]
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: State of a position that is not part of the valid sequence is never read as history.
  choices:
  - what: precision and layout of stored state
    engines: 5
  seen_in: [strata, ds4, hyperqwen, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: recurrent-state-store
  group: sequence-state
  summary: 'Hold state that is fixed in size and overwritten as the sequence advances, with what is needed to go back: snapshots,
    a second copy, one slot per proposed position, or a commit deferred until acceptance is known.'
  needed_when: The model has state that cannot be cut back to an earlier position, such as recurrent or convolution state.
  takes:
  - state updates from the computation
  gives:
  - current state
  - the means to return to the last accepted position
  owns_state:
  - the recurrent state and what is kept to go back
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact, numeric]
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: After proposed tokens are rejected, the state continues from the last accepted position.
  choices:
  - what: precision of stored state
    engines: 3
  seen_in: [strata, ds4, hyperqwen, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: state-pool
  group: sequence-state
  summary: 'Own the memory that sequences'' state shares: lay it out in pages, hand pages out and take them back, track
    who owns each, compact, and let shared pages be read by several sequences.'
  needed_when: Several sequences are in the engine at once and share one backing memory for state.
  takes:
  - requests for pages
  - releases
  gives:
  - pages
  - who may read or write each
  owns_state:
  - ownership, reference counts and the free list
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact, approximate]
  indirect_effect: true
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: A page is never written on behalf of a sequence that no longer owns it.
  choices:
  - what: page geometry shared by kinds of state of different sizes
    engines: 2
  - what: when fragmented space is compacted and emptied memory returned
    engines: 2
  seen_in: [hyperqwen, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: state-tiering
  group: sequence-state
  summary: Move per-sequence state out of fast memory to a slower place and back, so that more sequences or longer contexts
    fit, or so that state evicted from fast memory is restored instead of recomputed.
  needed_when: State in fast memory exceeds what fits, for long contexts or many sequences.
  takes:
  - state chosen to leave fast memory
  - requests to bring state back
  gives:
  - state restored where the computation reads it
  owns_state:
  - what is on the slower tier
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact, numeric, defines]
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: State brought back is the state that left, or the read is reported failed and nothing computed from it is committed.
  choices:
  - what: the tier's size and write budget
    engines: 2
  - what: chunking and staging of copies between tiers
    engines: 2
  seen_in: [strata, hyperqwen, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: prefix-reuse
  group: sequence-state
  summary: Find stored state that a new or resumed request can continue from, and make the sequence hold exactly that state.
  takes:
  - the request's tokens
  - stored state and what it is valid for
  gives:
  - the position reading continues from
  - restored state
  owns_state:
  - the stored states with what each is valid for, and an index of them where one is kept
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact, numeric, approximate]
  rules:
  - strength: should
    rule: Stored state is reused only where the model, the weights' precision, the settings and the prefix match what it
      was made for.
  choices:
  - what: when state is stored for later reuse, and where restore points exist when state cannot be truncated
    engines: 5
  - what: how many stored states are kept, and what is evicted first
    engines: 4
  - what: when restoring is refused in favour of reading again
    engines: 2
  - what: which store is used when several hold a match
    engines: 2
  - what: 'what earns stored state its retention: recency, cost to rebuild, or actual reuse'
    engines: 2
  seen_in: [strata, ds4, hyperqwen, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: session-persistence
  group: sequence-state
  summary: Write a sequence's whole state to a file and read it back, on request or when a store of reusable state asks
    for it.
  needed_when: The engine offers saving and restoring sessions.
  takes:
  - a sequence's state
  gives:
  - a file
  - a restored sequence
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact, numeric, approximate]
  rules:
  - strength: should
    rule: A file is loaded only where its recorded identity matches the model and settings.
  seen_in: [strata, ds4, llama-cpp]
- id: draft-proposal
  group: speculation
  summary: Cheaply propose the next few tokens, and when needed their probabilities, for the full model to check.
  not: Deciding whether to draft at all, or skipping the proposer when another source suffices, is the draft policy's job.
  needed_when: 'A cheap source of proposals exists: a draft head of the model, a separate small model, or repetition in
    the text.'
  forms:
  - a draft head of the model
  - a separate draft model
  - lookup of earlier text
  - several sources fused per position
  takes:
  - hidden features or recent tokens
  - how many to propose
  gives:
  - proposed tokens
  - their proposal probabilities, when acceptance needs them
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact, numeric, distribution_exact, approximate]
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: A proposed token is never returned to the client before the full model has accepted it.
  choices:
  - what: how many per round
    engines: 3
  - what: when a chain of proposals stops
    engines: 3
  - what: greedy or sampled proposals
    engines: 4
  - what: the set of tokens proposals are restricted to, and whether a cheaper reduced output head is used
    engines: 4
  - what: what the proposer needs before it may propose, and what is done when it cannot cover the context
    engines: 2
  - what: 'how a lookup source matches earlier text: how far back it searches, the shortest match it extends on, and how
      many tokens it may append'
    engines: 2
  seen_in: [strata, ds4, hyperqwen, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: draft-policy
  group: speculation
  summary: Decide each round whether to draft, from which source, and how many proposed tokens are sent for checking.
  needed_when: The amount of drafting is adjusted while running.
  takes:
  - acceptance results
  - the cost of a round
  gives:
  - the next round's size and source
  owns_state:
  - 'the signals it decides from: estimates of acceptance and cost, or the current mode and what ends it'
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact]
  indirect_effect: true
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: Its choices within a round never change the rule by which a token is accepted. A mode of the policy that requires
      another acceptance rule is stated with that mode.
  choices:
  - what: decisions per sequence or jointly across sequences sharing a step
    engines: 2
  seen_in: [strata, ds4, hyperqwen, splash]
- id: draft-verification
  group: speculation
  summary: Decide how many proposed tokens the full model accepts, and see that every kind of state comes to reflect exactly
    that prefix, by committing it or by giving each state's owner the accepted count.
  needed_when: Tokens are proposed ahead.
  forms:
  - acceptance and commit in one part
  - acceptance, then a separate commit after the accepted prefix has been shortened by stop conditions
  takes:
  - the full model's logits for the proposed positions
  - the proposals and, under sampling, their probabilities
  gives:
  - the accepted tokens
  - the accepted count by which each kind of state is committed, here or by the state's owner
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact, numeric, distribution_exact, approximate]
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: All state read as history reflects the accepted prefix; state of rejected positions may remain only if it is overwritten
      before any read.
  choices:
  - what: the acceptance rule under sampling
    engines: 4
  seen_in: [strata, ds4, hyperqwen, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: sampling
  group: token-output
  summary: Turn each position's logits into one token by a chain of steps, with the settings that apply at that position.
  takes:
  - logits
  - the request's sampling settings
  - any mask from an output constraint
  gives:
  - the chosen token
  - its probabilities, when asked
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact, numeric, distribution_exact, defines]
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: With a fixed seed, fixed logits and, under speculation, fixed proposals, it returns the same token.
  choices:
  - what: limits on candidates considered
    engines: 2
  - what: the kernel used for the sampling arithmetic, and how it changes with the number of rows
    engines: 2
  - what: the default values of the settings
    engines: 2
  seen_in: [strata, ds4, hyperqwen, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: output-constraint
  group: token-output
  summary: 'Restrict or force which tokens may come next, from a rule outside the model: a grammar, a tool-call format,
    a budget.'
  not: Changing sampling settings per position without forbidding any token is sampling, not a constraint.
  needed_when: The service offers constrained output, or a format that must be enforced.
  takes:
  - the rule
  - the tokens produced so far
  gives:
  - a mask or forced tokens for the next position
  owns_state:
  - per-sequence position in the rule
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact, defines]
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: A token the rule forbids is never returned.
  choices:
  - what: which requests a rule is applied to, and which constraint languages may be combined
    engines: 2
  seen_in: [hyperqwen, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: output-interpretation
  group: token-output
  summary: 'Turn produced tokens into what is returned: text, the split between reasoning, answer and tool calls, and the
    decision where the output stops.'
  takes:
  - produced tokens
  - the request's stop conditions and limits
  gives:
  - text and structured parts
  - the point at which generation ends
  owns_state:
  - per-request parse position
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact, defines]
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: Text is not returned while it could still turn out to be part of a stop sequence.
  choices:
  - what: a budget on the reasoning part, and what is done when it is reached
    engines: 3
  - what: reasoning and tool formats per model family, and how tool calls are parsed or repaired
    engines: 4
  seen_in: [strata, ds4, hyperqwen, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: request-front
  group: serving
  summary: Accept requests over the protocols offered, hold the connection, and return results.
  takes:
  - client requests
  gives:
  - requests for the engine
  - responses to the client
  owns_state:
  - connections, and stored responses where the engine offers them
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact]
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: A request is accepted only from callers the deployment allows. An engine with no caller check of its own says

  choices:
  - what: who is allowed and how
    engines: 2
  - what: limits on connections, body size and queue
    engines: 3
  seen_in: [strata, ds4, hyperqwen, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: prompt-preparation
  group: serving
  summary: Turn a request's messages, tools and settings into the exact prompt tokens.
  takes:
  - messages, tools and settings
  gives:
  - prompt tokens and the token limit
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact, defines]
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: Token ids come from the model's vocabulary, and the sequence is the tokenizer's output for the whole text or a

    engines: 3
  - what: keeping the start of the prompt stable so that stored state can be reused

  - what: whether the prompt is tokenized whole or in pieces joined at a reuse boundary
    engines: 3
  seen_in: [strata, ds4, hyperqwen, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: step-scheduler
  group: serving
  summary: 'Run the engine''s loop: decide each cycle what the next step contains, which sequences join it, and what waits.'
  not: Running the process loop without deciding what a step contains is engine supervision. A loop that decides which sequences
    advance in each step is a step scheduler, even when it is also the process loop.
  takes:
  - waiting and running sequences
  - what each needs next
  gives:
  - the plan of the next step
  owns_state:
  - queues of sequences and their turn
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact]
  indirect_effect: true
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: Every admitted sequence is eventually served or ended with an explicit error. Where the engine bounds the wait,
      the bound is stated.
  choices:
  - what: whether prompt reading and generation share a step
    engines: 2
  - what: sequences and rows per step
    engines: 2
  - what: how a long prompt yields to generation in progress
    engines: 2
  - what: the order of work within one cycle
    engines: 2
  seen_in: [strata, ds4, hyperqwen, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: sequence-lifecycle
  group: serving
  summary: 'Own each sequence''s life in the engine: admit it, give it a place, keep the record of the tokens whose state
    is live, pause and resume it, and release it.'
  takes:
  - a request for the engine
  - what is free
  gives:
  - an admitted sequence with a place
  - its record of committed tokens
  owns_state:
  - per-sequence record and place
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact]
  indirect_effect: true
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: The record of committed tokens matches the state held for the sequence, or the sequence is marked invalid and
      its state is not read until rebuilt.
  choices:
  - what: which running sequence gives way when resources run short, and which place is repurposed first
    engines: 3
  seen_in: [strata, ds4, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: replica-routing
  group: serving
  summary: Present several independent copies of the engine as one, and choose which copy serves each request.
  needed_when: Several whole copies of the engine run side by side.
  takes:
  - requests
  - the load and state of each copy
  gives:
  - the copy that serves a request
  owns_state:
  - what each copy is doing and what state it holds
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact]
  indirect_effect: true
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: A request continues on a copy that holds its state, or its state is rebuilt before it continues.
  seen_in: [strata, llama-cpp]
- id: engine-supervision

  not: Deciding what each step contains is the step scheduler's job, also where one loop does both.
  forms:
  - one engine process
  - one worker process per device or rank, started, watched and stopped together
  takes:
  - start and stop commands
  - liveness signals
  gives:
  - a running engine
  - failure reports
  owns_state:
  - the engine's start stage and health
  effect_on_output: [bit_exact, defines]
  indirect_effect: true
  rules:
  - strength: must
    rule: A request is not sent to an engine that has not finished starting.
  choices:
  - what: the stages of a start and what is retried
    engines: 2
  - what: when the engine counts as stalled or failed
    engines: 2
  - what: when an idle engine is unloaded
    engines: 2
  - what: after how many failures in what time the engine is not started again, and the wait between restarts
    engines: 2
  seen_in: [strata, hyperqwen, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: scoring
  group: serving

  seen_in: [ds4, hyperqwen, ninfer, llama-cpp]
- id: configuration
  group: operations
  summary: Turn the operator's choices and the machine's facts into one validated set of settings, and refuse combinations
    the engine does not support or that are known to give wrong output.

  - what the machine is

  indirect_effect: true

  choices:
  - what: operator values, presets, measured values and defaults
    engines: 2
  - what: rules that derive a setting's default from other settings and machine facts

  - what: which of the machine's devices the engine may use, and how they are identified to it
    engines: 2
  seen_in: [strata, ds4, hyperqwen, ninfer, splash, llama-cpp]
- id: resource-governing
  group: operations
  summary: 'While the engine runs, keep its use of memory or power within limits: admit or refuse what is asked for, and
    take back from holders in a fixed order when the limit tightens.'
  needed_when: 'What the engine may use changes while it runs: the system reclaims memory, sequences come and go, or power
    is limited.'
  forms:
  - 'memory: grants and reclaim among the holders of memory'
  - 'duty cycle: idle time inserted to hold a power or heat level'
  takes:
  - requests for memory
  - what the system reports about pressure
  - for duty cycle, the target level and measured work
  gives:
  - grants and refusals
  - requests to holders to give memory back
  - for duty cycle, inserted idle time
  owns_state:

  effect_on_output: [bit_exact]
  indirect_effect: true
  rules:

    rule: A grant of memory never takes the engine over a hard limit. A soft figure is exceeded only by classes of work
      the engine states in advance, or on the operator's explicit choice.
